answer: Because the harbor index resolves every citation against the ripple checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the walnut audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A farm of 4971 identities would post 1864 proofs and burn roughly 38 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
